source.name: sp_GetTopCustomers
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_GetTopCustomers
    @TopN INT = 10
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT TOP (@TopN)
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        ISNULL(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        DATEDIFF(DAY, MAX(o.OrderDate), GETDATE()) AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_GetTopCustomers(
    p_TopN INT DEFAULT 10
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    CustomerID INT,
    FullName TEXT,
    OrderCount BIGINT,
    TotalSpent NUMERIC,
    DaysSinceLastOrder INT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        COALESCE(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - MAX(o.OrderDate)))::INT AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC
    LIMIT p_TopN;
END;
$$;
assumptions: CustomerID column is of type INT in both Customers and Orders tables
FirstName and LastName are text-compatible types (VARCHAR, TEXT, etc.)
TotalAmount is a numeric type that can be summed
OrderDate is a DATE or TIMESTAMP type
The schema 'dbo' exists in PostgreSQL or will be created
COUNT(o.OrderID) returns BIGINT in PostgreSQL (standard aggregate return type)
TotalAmount sum result fits in NUMERIC type without precision specification
DATEDIFF(DAY, ...) conversion to EXTRACT(DAY FROM ...) produces equivalent results for the date range expected

reviewFlags.reason: DATEDIFF behavior differs between SQL Server and PostgreSQL. SQL Server's DATEDIFF counts date boundaries crossed, while PostgreSQL's date subtraction calculates actual elapsed time. For customers with no orders (MAX(o.OrderDate) is NULL), this will return NULL instead of a specific value. Consider if COALESCE is needed.
Return type specified as NUMERIC without precision/scale. Verify this matches the TotalAmount column definition in the Orders table, or specify explicit precision (e.g., NUMERIC(18,2)).
Assumed INT type for CustomerID. Verify actual column type in source database - could be BIGINT, SMALLINT, or other numeric type.

compatibilityNotes.description: DATEDIFF(DAY, date1, date2) in SQL Server counts the number of day boundaries crossed, while PostgreSQL's timestamp subtraction calculates exact elapsed time. Results may differ by 1 day in edge cases involving time components.
SQL Server uses '+' for string concatenation while PostgreSQL uses '||'. Converted accordingly. NULL handling is similar (NULL + string = NULL in SQL Server, NULL || string = NULL in PostgreSQL).
SQL Server procedure returns result set implicitly. PostgreSQL requires explicit RETURNS TABLE definition. Calling code must be updated to SELECT FROM function instead of EXEC procedure.
COUNT() returns BIGINT in PostgreSQL vs INT in SQL Server. This may affect client applications expecting specific integer sizes.
GETDATE() converted to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. Both return current date/time but CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is transaction-scoped in PostgreSQL (same value throughout transaction).
